plan.contextChunk: This figure combines a ray construction with an intensity curve for light passing through a single slit. At the left a vertical tan barrier is drawn in two segments with a narrow gap between them; a double-headed arrow spans the gap and a curved arrow connects it to the label a. A short teal arrow labeled lambda enters horizontally from the left and reaches the opening. From the slit five gray dashed lines fan out to the right toward a vertical gray line labeled Screen, and the middle dashed line runs straight along the horizontal. Two arcs measure angles from that horizontal reference: the outer upper line is marked theta_2 = 45 degrees and the inner upper line is marked theta_1 = ?, with two more dashed lines mirroring them below the axis. Drawn on the screen is a red wavy curve, tied by a curved arrow to the label Intensity on screen, whose sideways excursion represents brightness; it has a tall broad central peak on the axis and smaller lobes above and below, and each dashed ray meets the screen exactly where the curve pinches in to nothing. Lining the ray directions up with the nulls of the curve identifies each dashed line with a numbered diffraction minimum, so that the known 45 degree direction can be used to recover the slit width a and then the unknown angle theta_1.

interactionPlan.concept: Single-slit diffraction minima occur where a·sin(θ) = m·λ, so the geometric ray directions to each dark fringe are exactly the zeros of the sinc² intensity curve on the screen, and the whole pattern's angular width scales as λ/a.
elements: vertical tan barrier drawn as two segments with a narrow central gap (the slit)
double-headed vertical arrow spanning the gap, labeled 'a' via a curved leader arrow
short teal horizontal arrow entering the slit from the left, labeled 'λ'
slit point at the gap center from which rays emanate
horizontal gray dashed reference line (θ = 0) from slit to screen
five gray dashed rays fanning to the screen at the m = -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 minimum directions
inner angle arc from the horizontal to the m = +1 ray, labeled 'θ₁ = ?'
outer angle arc from the horizontal to the m = +2 ray, labeled 'θ₂ = 45°'
vertical gray line on the right labeled 'Screen'
red sideways intensity curve (sinc² pattern) drawn on the screen: tall broad central peak on the axis with smaller side lobes above and below
null markers where each non-zero dashed ray meets the screen, coinciding with the intensity curve pinching to zero
label 'Intensity on screen' with a curved leader arrow pointing at the red curve

interactions.label: Slit width a
interactions.teaches: Widening the slit (a ↑) pulls every minimum ray and intensity null toward the axis, compressing the pattern — the angular spacing of fringes is inversely proportional to a.

interactions.label: Wavelength λ
interactions.teaches: Increasing the wavelength (λ ↑) pushes the minimum rays and intensity nulls outward, spreading the pattern — fringe spacing is directly proportional to λ, making a·sin(θ) = m·λ visible as the rays track the curve's zeros.

Clicking a dashed ray (or its screen null) highlights that ray and the matching zero-intensity pinch together, revealing that the geometric diffraction angle and the dark fringe of the intensity curve are the same physical condition a·sin(θ) = m·λ.

demo_steps.title: Rays meet the nulls
demo_steps.narration: Each gray dashed ray points exactly at a place where the red intensity curve pinches to zero on the screen — the ray directions and the dark fringes are one and the same set of angles.

demo_steps.title: Widen the slit
demo_steps.narration: Drag the slit-width slider up: all minimum rays and intensity nulls swing inward toward the axis and the central peak narrows, showing that a wider opening produces a tighter diffraction pattern.

demo_steps.title: Lengthen the wavelength
demo_steps.narration: Now drag the wavelength slider toward red: the rays and nulls swing back outward and the lobes widen, showing that longer light diffracts more — the pattern width tracks λ/a.

demo_steps.title: Tie angle to zero
demo_steps.narration: Click the m = 1 ray (θ₁) and its screen null to highlight them as a pair; the highlighted angle satisfies a·sin(θ₁) = λ, the same equation that forces the intensity to zero there.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The dashed ray directions and the zeros of the on-screen intensity curve are identical — both are the minima condition a·sin(θ) = m·λ — so the diffraction pattern's angular width is set by the single ratio λ/a.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Left-to-right layout: tan vertical barrier with a small central gap on the left; a teal horizontal arrow labeled λ pointing into the gap and a double-headed vertical arrow across the gap labeled a via a curved leader. From the gap center, five gray dashed rays fan rightward (m = -2,-1,0,+1,2) plus the horizontal θ=0 reference; near the slit draw two concentric angle arcs labeled θ₁ = ? (inner, to m=+1) and θ₂ = 45° (outer, to m=+2). On the right, a vertical gray line labeled Screen carries a red sinc² curve drawn sideways (horizontal excursion = brightness): one tall broad central lobe on the axis and decaying side lobes above and below, with each non-zero ray landing exactly on a pinch-to-zero null. A curved leader arrow tags the red curve as 'Intensity on screen'. Keep rays gray and thin, the intensity curve a saturated red, and highlight a selected ray+null pair in a contrasting accent color on click. Recompute ray angles as θ_m = arcsin(m·λ/a) and redraw both rays and the sinc² curve whenever a or λ changes so the alignment is always exact.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for slit width a: learner changes the opening while lambda stays fixed; the dashed minimum directions and red intensity nulls spread apart or compress; the inverse relationship between slit width and diffraction-pattern angular spacing becomes clear.
- Slider for wavelength lambda: learner changes the incoming wavelength; the intensity lobes and minimum angles shift outward for longer wavelengths and inward for shorter ones; the condition a sin(theta)=m lambda becomes visible on the screen.
- Click on a diffraction minimum: learner selects theta_1, theta_2, or its mirrored counterpart; the corresponding dashed ray and zero-intensity pinch point highlight together; the alignment between geometric angles and zeros of the intensity curve becomes clear.

authoredContext:
Calculating Single-Slit Diffraction Visible light of wavelength 550 nm falls on a single slit and produces its second diffraction minimum at an angle of 45.0° relative to the incident direction of the light, as in the figure. (a) What is the width of the slit? (b) At what angle is the first minimum produced?

In this example, we analyze a graph of the single-slit diffraction pattern.

Figure shows a vertical line on the left. This has a slit in the middle, of length a. A ray labeled lambda passes horizontally through the slit. This splits into 5 dotted lines that fall on a screen. The screen is shown as a vertical line. Of the five dotted lines, two make angles theta 1 and theta 2 with the horizontal. Theta 2 is 45 degrees. Theta 1 is smaller than theta 2 and is unknown. Intensity on the screen is shown as a vertical wave. The crest at the center, where a horizontal dotted line from the center of the slit falls on the screen, is the largest. The wave attenuates at the top and bottom. The remaining four dotted lines correspond to troughs in the wave.

Strategy From the given information, and assuming the screen is far away from the slit, we can use the equation asinθ=mλ first to find D, and again to find the angle for the first minimum θ1.

discrepancies: The source shows θ₁ = ? (a pedagogical question for the student to solve), while the generated figure displays a computed value θ₁ = 20.6°, removing the problem-solving element of the original
The source shows θ₂ = 45° exactly, while the generated figure shows θ₂ = 44.8° due to the chosen parameter values (a=1.56 μm, λ=550 nm), a minor numerical mismatch
The source intensity curve shows more complete secondary maxima (side lobes) above and below the central peak; the generated figure's vertical extent clips some of the outer lobes
evaluation.notes: The generated figure faithfully reproduces the single-slit diffraction diagram with correct physics (sinc² intensity, minima at a·sinθ=mλ, rays aligned to nulls) and adds excellent interactivity (slit-width and wavelength sliders, click-to-highlight, demo steps), but replaces the source's pedagogical θ₁=? question with a computed value and shows slightly truncated side lobes.
action_items: Consider showing θ₁ = ? in the default (step 0) state to preserve the source's problem-solving intent, then revealing the computed value in later demo steps or on interaction

Adjust the vertical extent of the intensity curve sampling range or reduce maxIW slightly so that at least two full side lobes are visible above and below the central maximum, matching the source's visual completeness
Fine-tune default parameters (e.g., a=1.556 μm) so that θ₂ computes to exactly 45.0° at the default state, matching the source annotation
